result.builder:
Goal: one pull request on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test that makes packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js accept several files and meets every line of https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104.

Context: right now packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js reads only process.argv[2], calls lint(text) from packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js and prints `<file>:<line>: <error>` (newlines in the error replaced by spaces). It exits 0 if clean, 1 if any row is bad, 2 if there is no argument or the file can't be read. Tests are in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (they spawn the bin with spawnSync) and packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js. Docs are in packages/jsonl-lint/README.md. Tools must stay zero-dependency plain ES modules on Node 22+, with node:test tests.

Steps:
1. Do not touch the lint(text) function in packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js. Leave that file byte-for-byte unchanged. Put all the new behaviour in the bin.
2. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js:
   - Args = process.argv.slice(2). If there are none, write a usage line to stderr (e.g. `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`, where `-` means stdin) and exit 2.
   - If `-` appears more than once, write a usage error to stderr and exit 2 before reading anything.
   - Go through the files in the order given. For `-`, read stdin (readFileSync(0, 'utf8')) and report it under the name `-`. For any other file, readFileSync(file, 'utf8'). If a read fails, write `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, remember the failure, and carry on with the next file. Do not exit early.
   - For each file that was read, print `<file>:<line>: <error>` for every problem from lint(text), exactly as the single-file version does: file name as given, error newlines replaced with spaces. All lines for one file come before the lines for the next file.
   - Exit code: 2 if any file couldn't be read, otherwise 1 if any row in any file was bad, otherwise 0. So an unreadable file plus a bad row gives 2.
   - A single file must behave exactly as before: same output, same exit codes, same stderr. Existing tests must still pass.
3. Add node:test tests to packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js. Feed stdin with spawnSync's `input` option. Cover:
   - two clean files: exit 0, no stdout
   - one bad file among several clean ones: exit 1, and only the bad file's `<file>:<line>: <error>` lines
   - a bad file between two others: output in argument order
   - stdin via `-`, clean: exit 0
   - stdin via `-`, bad: exit 1, lines start with `-:`
   - a missing file among good or bad ones: exit 2, error on stderr, and the other files still reported on stdout
   - two `-` arguments: exit 2, stderr not empty
   - no arguments: exit 2, usage on stderr
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md:
   - Usage: `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`. Files are checked in order, `-` means stdin and is reported as `-`, and `-` may appear only once.
   - Exit codes: 0 if every file is clean; 1 if any row in any file is bad; 2 if no file is named, `-` is given twice, or any file can't be read. In the last case the error goes to stderr and the other files are still checked.
5. Run `npm test` at the repo root and make sure it passes. Also try the CLI by hand on a few combinations.
6. Open one PR. Its body must contain the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) to pass at the PR head. If it fails, fix it and push again.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 at its head commit. Check out the head, run `npm ci` at the repository root, and run each check below in order. For the CLI checks, make a temporary directory with these files: a.jsonl = `{"a":1}\n{"b":2}\n` (clean), b.jsonl = `{"c":3}\n` (clean), bad.jsonl = `{"a":1}\n{oops}\n` (bad row 2). BIN = packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js. After every command, record stdout, stderr and the exit status (`echo $?`).

Check 1. Expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before".
Run `node BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl b.jsonl`, then `node BIN bad.jsonl a.jsonl bad2.jsonl`, where bad2.jsonl is a copy of bad.jsonl. Then run `node BIN bad.jsonl` on its own.
PASS: in each multi-file run, every bad row of every named file appears as `<file>:<line>: <error>` with the file name as given. Output for an earlier argument comes before output for a later one: bad.jsonl's line before bad2.jsonl's. The single-file run prints `bad.jsonl:2: <error>`.
FAIL: a file named after the first is not checked, a bad row is missing or in the wrong format, or the order does not follow the arguments.

Check 2. Expect line: "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)".
Run `printf '{oops}\n' | node BIN -` and `printf '{"a":1}\n' | node BIN a.jsonl -`. Then run `printf '{"a":1}\n' | node BIN - -`.
PASS: the first run prints a line beginning `-:1: `. The second run prints no problem lines. The `- -` run exits 2.
FAIL: stdin is not read, it is reported under some name other than `-`, or `- -` does not exit 2.

Check 3. Expect line: "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)".
Run:
(a) `node BIN a.jsonl b.jsonl` — expect exit 0
(b) `node BIN a.jsonl bad.jsonl b.jsonl` — expect exit 1
(c) `node BIN` — expect exit 2
(d) `node BIN a.jsonl missing.jsonl bad.jsonl` — expect exit 2, a non-empty stderr that mentions the error, and stdout still containing `bad.jsonl:2: ...`
PASS: all four behave as expected.
FAIL: any wrong exit status; (d) has nothing on stderr; or (d) does not report bad.jsonl.

Check 4. Expect line: "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged".
Run `git diff <merge-base with main>..HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` and read the file at the head.
PASS: the lint function's signature and body are identical to the base.
FAIL: the lint(text) function differs in any way.

Check 5. Expect line: "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage".
Read the test files under packages/jsonl-lint/test/ at the head and run `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint`. Read packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.
PASS: there are node:test tests for each of these cases, and they pass:
- two clean files
- one bad file among several
- stdin via `-`, clean
- stdin via `-`, bad
- a missing file among good ones
- two `-` arguments
- no arguments
The README also documents multi-file usage, including `-`.
FAIL: any of those cases has no test, a test fails, or the README does not document the new usage.

Check 6. Expect line: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head".
Run `gh pr view <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid,state`, `gh pr checks <pr>`, and `npm test` at the repo root.
PASS: the body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, the `test` workflow check passes at the head SHA, and `npm test` exits 0 locally.
FAIL: any of these is missing or failing.

Advisory (not pass/fail):
- Check that the exact single-file output and stderr match the previous version.
- Check that `- -` fails before reading stdin.
- Check that an unreadable file plus a bad row exits 2, not 1.
- Check that stderr for a missing file uses the `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: ...` form.
